newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Malaysia in combo deal, Thais buy soybeans - trade.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia in combo deal, Thais buy soybeans - trade.

text.p: Malaysia's Soon Soon Bhd recently clinched a deal for a combination cargo of corn and soybeans, while an oil crusher in Thailand bought 50,000 tonnes of soybeans from Brazil, traders said on Wednesday.
Soon Soon's purchase was for prompt May shipment on a Panamax, they said.
"The deal was done last week," a dealer in Singapore said.
The price of the corn bought by Soon Soon was estimated by the trade at around US$141-$142 a tonne C&F. The soybeans were seen at around $340-$341 a tonne C&F.
The Malaysians apparently got a discount since Argentine corn coming into Southeast Asia was seen by the trade at around $144-$146 a tonne C&F on a Panamax for June/July shipment.
Thai Vegetable Oil, on the other hand, bought 50,000 tonnes of Brazilian soybeans for June delivery, Thai traders said.

Singapore-based dealers could not determine the price of the purchase but said the price of Brazilian soybeans coming into Southeast Asia should fetch a quote of about $330-$350 a tonne C&F on a Panamax for May/July shipment.
U.S. soybeans, however, were quoted at $338-$340 a tonne C&F on a Panamax for June/July shipment.

The rest of the regional grain and oilseeds market was quiet, but a senior European dealer predicted business will perk up if Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) futures prices slip further over the next few days.
"The market needs a dip and then people will come in," one said. "It's extremely quiet, but buyers are not well-covered."
Open positions for soymeal in June have apparently been rolled forward by some buyers into July or August on the belief prices will still come off, dealers said.
"I think most of the meal buyers will be waiting for July," a trader said, adding he expects Indonesia to buy about 50,000-100,000 tonnes of meal.
Malaysia was also said to be looking for another 20,000 tonnes of soymeal for July shipment, the dealers said.

Brazilian soymeal still enjoyed a discount to U.S. meal. It was quoted by regional dealers at around $330-$335 a tonne C&F on a Panamax for June/July shipment, while U.S. soymeal was seen at $343-$345 a tonne C&F on the same basis.
While some people in the trade were still making offers for Chinese corn, buyers were seen preferring Argentine origins.
"The Chinese are still around, but for the big boys Argentine corn is better than Chinese corn," one dealer said.
Chinese corn was seen by the trade $146-$148 a tonne C&F on a Handy for June/July shipment. U.S. corn, on the other hand, fetched a quote of $149-$150 a tonne C&F on the same basis.
Most Southeast Asian buyers, though, seem to prefer waiting for prices to come off in the next few weeks.
"There's no urgency to buy for people in the business," a dealer said. "It's pretty quiet."
